clue.text: One slip ruined character

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper form, so the letters must be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single mistake has ruined somebody's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as reputation, but here it means a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Increase the wealth of Henri Christophe to some extent

indicators.note: taking only part of the words, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: found spanning the two names

explanation.surface: Henri Christophe, the king of Haiti, was made somewhat richer.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Christophe was a leader of the Haitian revolution who crowned himself king.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich someone is to make them richer, adding to their money and possessions.

clue.text: Cross sailor has to overcome anger

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An irritable sailor must get his temper under control.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the sailor sits above the anger, overcoming it. 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross in heraldry, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Tomato has nothing on fruit

parts.note: love is zero in a tennis score
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A tomato has nothing over other fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an old name for the tomato, once thought to be an aphrodisiac.

clue.text: It's not usual seeing one endlessly remain covered in ointment

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is wrapped by it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic ointment from ancient times

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
to stand is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: It is odd to see someone stay coated in cream forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Nard is a fragrant balm mentioned in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonstandard departs from the norm, so it is not usual or regular.

clue.text: Man given silver cup as prize

parts.note: Jack is a common man's name, and jack also means a man or fellow
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy, typically a silver cup

explanation.surface: A man is presented with a silver cup as his award.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or gambling game, the main reward to be won.

clue.text: Simpleton always sought after justice

indicators.note: coming after means this piece follows the other one in the order of the letters

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Justice, a judge's title
ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A simple fellow keeps looking for justice.
explanation.walkthrough: The jay, a chattering bird, gave its name to a foolish talker.
explanation.definitionFit: A jay is a dated term for a gullible or foolish person, a simpleton.

clue.text: Expenses of constructing road in island

indicators.note: one thing found in another is held inside it, so these letters are placed within

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island
St is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: The bill for building a road on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs are the amounts that must be paid out for something, its expenses or outlays.

clue.text: Bill's in mountain-climbing club, say

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a club is one of the four suits of playing card, so an example of a card

explanation.surface: Bill is a member of the local mountaineering society.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is the noun for a posted notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed public notice or poster, the same thing as a placard.

clue.text: Cheap sheepfold near city

parts.note: split in two: a tup is a ram, a male sheep, and a fold is an enclosure, a pen
NY is New York

explanation.surface: An inexpensive sheep enclosure close to town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepfold' must be split into its two halves. Tuppenny means costing two old British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppenny, worth just twopence, is used to mean cheap or of little value.

clue.text: Bearing in car evenly adjusted

indicators.note: adjusting something moves its parts about, so the letters are set in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wheel bearing in a car has been tuned so it runs evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a mechanical part, but it means connection, as in 'has a bearing on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a bearing on a matter means being connected or pertinent to it, which is relevancy.

clue.text: Slough traffic skirting motorway

indicators.note: to skirt something is to run round its edge, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to traffic is to trade or exchange, to swap
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Traffic in the town of Slough runs round the edge of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London beside the M4, but here it is the ordinary noun for a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy, waterlogged area of ground, the same thing as a swamp or marsh.

clue.text: Country having India, Nepal Afghanistan providing entry points

definitions.text: Country having India, Nepal Afghanistan providing entry points

indicators.note: the entry point of a word is where you go in, its opening letter, so only the initials count

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A country borders India, Nepal and Afghanistan, which give it ways in.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes China, which does border all three; read for wordplay, the initials of its first five words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the large East Asian nation whose land frontier touches India, Nepal and Afghanistan.

clue.text: A Lowry, for instance, that ultimately has point

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of that
to have something is to own it
a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A painting by Lowry, it turns out, does have a point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter known for scenes of northern industrial towns crowded with matchstick figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lowry painting typically depicts an urban scene, and a picture of a town is a townscape.

clue.text: Cleaning lady who wears out bishop, perhaps

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a bishop is an example of a chess piece, or man

explanation.surface: A charwoman exhausts the bishop she works for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears out' looks like one phrasal verb; split it, so 'out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A washerwoman is a woman who washes other people's clothes for a living, a laundress.

clue.text: Practise how to conceal cards?

parts.note: the setter's reading: keep up a skill by doing it regularly
the surface reading: a card player hiding what they hold by keeping it close in the palm

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes keeping cards held out of sight, but idiomatically it means staying in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means continuing to do something occasionally so as not to lose the skill, which is practising.

clue.text: White flower covered by rising lake

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A pale bloom floats beneath the swelling waters of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the flower sits beneath the reversed lake, so it is covered by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth translucent white stone, so the word is used for pure whiteness.

clue.text: What mimic does suddenly becomes popular

definitions.meaning: first meaning: imitates someone, often to mock them
second meaning: a product or career that rapidly succeeds

explanation.surface: An impressionist's act abruptly becomes a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to parody someone's manner and to start succeeding rapidly, like an aircraft climbing.

clue.text: Sees yacht abeam — manoeuvres according to circumstances

indicators.note: a yacht that manoeuvres shifts about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a yacht alongside and steers to suit the conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean depending on whatever situation turns out to apply, matching circumstances.

clue.text: In that article restraint is necessary

parts.note: the is the definite article
a rein is a check or restraint

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece calls for self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In that article' reads as one phrase about a piece of writing; split it after 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning in that place or in that matter.

clue.text: Club that's after money

indicators.note: coming after places this piece behind the other in the letter order

parts.note: brass is northern English slang for money
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A society whose members are only interested in wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a two-wood golf club, once fitted with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: Carefree shout conceals a lot of care

indicators.note: something that conceals another hides it inside, so the other word goes within

parts.note: to cry is to shout

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: heed means care or attention

explanation.surface: A light-hearted yell hides deep concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery person is in good spirits, untroubled and light-hearted, which is close to carefree.

clue.text: Watches the way in which commercial's presented make-up

parts.note: to watch is to eye

indicators.note: something presented in a setting sits inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: how means the way in which something happens
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone notices how a cosmetics advert shows off its products.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after commercial is read as 'is', so the advertisement is set inside the phrase meaning the way in which.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a cosmetic coloured powder put on the eyelids, one kind of make-up.

clue.text: Man upset woman's beauty preparation

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name, and the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A man ruins a woman's cosmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the woman is turned over; the man stays as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a shrub, used to colour hair and decorate skin.

clue.text: Cause embarrassment to sailor like Henry

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman
as means like
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of electrical inductance

explanation.surface: A seaman such as Henry is made to feel awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name, but it is the scientific unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel ashamed or self-conscious, causing embarrassment.

clue.text: Main ring may see entrance of equestriennes at first

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: a word that sees another enter takes it inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: may and can both express permission

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is taken
at first repeats the signal that only the beginning of the word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of equestriennes

explanation.surface: In the central circus ring, female riders may be seen coming in first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' doubles the hint that only the opening letter is wanted. The main is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main, short for the main sea, is a literary term for the open sea or ocean.

clue.text: A little coffee set is made to be broken

indicators.note: a broken item has its pieces scattered, so the letters fall into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dainty coffee service seems designed to be smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffee set' reads as a phrase, but the definition stops at coffee and 'set' starts the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee served after dinner, so a little serving.

clue.text: Colouring of stamp being discussed

indicators.note: something being discussed is spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a die is a stamp for impressing a design on coins or metal

explanation.surface: The colour of a postage stamp is under debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' suggests postage, but it is the minting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye is a substance used to colour cloth, hair or other material, a colouring.

clue.text: Flourish on cool food

parts.note: to fan is to cool by moving air
fare is food provided, as in good plain fare

explanation.surface: Someone waves a hand grandly over chilled food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' looks like a verb meaning thrive, but it is the noun for a showy burst of trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short ceremonial tune played on brass, also called a flourish of trumpets.

clue.text: Place to grow plant that is tender and rosy on the outside

parts.note: to nurse is to tend the sick, and a tender is one who tends

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is wanted, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of rosy

explanation.surface: A greenhouse spot for a delicate plant with pink outer petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective for a fragile plant, but it is the noun for someone who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants and trees are raised for sale or transplanting.
